paper.title: An algorithm with nearly optimal pseudo-regret for both stochastic and adversarial bandits

settings.definition_quote: In a stochastic multi-armed bandit problem the rewards for each arm~$i$ are generated by a fixed but unknown probability distribution $\nu_i$ on~$[0,1]$. All rewards $x_i(t)$ ... are generated independently at random with $x_i(t) \sim \nu_i$.
If the selection of rewards $x_i(t)$, $1 \leq i \leq K$, depends on which arms $I_1,\ldots,I_{t-1}$ the player has chosen in the past, then the adversary is called {\em adaptive}.

source.label: theorem_lower_bound
source.quote: Let $\alpha < 1$, $\epsilon > 0$, $\beta < 2$, and $\clower > 0$. Consider a player that achieves pseudo-regret $\pseudoR_\sto(n) \leq \clower (\log n)^\beta$ for any stochastic bandit problem with two arms and gap~$\Delta=1/8$. Then for large enough $n$ there is an adversarial bandit problem with two arms and an oblivious adversary such that the player suffers regret $R_\obl(n) \geq n^\alpha/8 - 4\sqrt{n \log n}$ with probability at least $1/(16n^{\epsilon}) - 2/n^2$.

results.notes: Regret holds with small (vanishing) probability, so recorded as realized_regret lower bound; probability field set to high_probability though it is a probability-at-least statement. Theorem number uncertain (counter possibly shared with cited Theorem t:EXP3).

conditions: player achieves stochastic pseudo-regret <= C (log n)^beta_lb, beta_lb < 2, on every two-armed stochastic problem with gap 1/8

source.label: theorem_lower_bound
source.quote: Furthermore, there is an adversarial bandit problem with two arms and an adaptive adversary such that the player suffers expected regret \[ \EE{R_\ada(n)} \geq \frac{n^{\alpha-\epsilon}}{128} - 3\sqrt{n \log n} . \]

results.notes: Shows no algorithm with O((log n)^beta), beta<2, stochastic pseudo-regret can have O~(sqrt n) expected regret against adaptive adversaries. Theorem number uncertain.
